collection.source_input: US9766437B2, prescription table 1 of 4 (the publication's own 'Example 1', confirmed: its lens data are the first table, the conditional-expression table's Example 1 column reproduces this prescription, and the surface count and group structure match the Example 1 description)
collection.redistribution: public patent document; the prescription numbers are transcribed as facts, no source asset is redistributed
collection.attribution: US9766437B2, Olympus Corporation; the design is cited by publication number and example

title: Endoscope objective optical system, US9766437B2 example 1, normal observation state

design.source_reference: US9766437B2 example 1, normal observation state (d0 = 19.8 mm, d1 = 0.29898 mm, d2 = 2.40541 mm)

aperture_validity.basis: the aperture stop is a plate at source surface 10 in the air space between the second group and the third group, with a derived opening radius of 0.482 mm inside a plate that reaches 0.740 mm, the clear radius of the surface beside it
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: eligibility only: a stop-dependent match needs evidence (a field point or pupil sample), which this batch does not assert

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED e line. The publication's lens data carry the index as ne and its text states that all values of focal length are about an e-line; the e line is 546.07 nm in air, converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact at 20 C and 101325 Pa)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states one index per surface, at the e line. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; a single e-line index per surface does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.note: the publication prints no effective focal length in millimetres. Its conditional-expression table gives only ratios of the focal length, which the engine's value reproduces (see engine_check.comparison.why), and a ratio is not a stated focal length, so no source value is recorded here

back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the image plane, which the source states as the last surface's spacing (surface 17, d = 0.792 mm)
back_focal_length_mm.conditions: normal observation state, object distance d0 = 19.8 mm; the image plane is the source's own IMG row

total_track_mm.definition: first surface vertex to the image plane along the axis: the sum of the source's stated spacings from surface 1 to the image plane

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length
comparison.why: the source states no effective focal length in millimetres, so the rule has no pair of source values to compare against, and the two quantities the engine reports are not both the source's: the engine's back focal length (0.773135 mm) is the rear focal distance for an object at infinity, while the source's 0.792 mm is the image distance at its own stated object distance d0 = 19.8 mm, so the two are different quantities and are not compared. What does check is the publication's conditional-expression table, which is independent of the object distance: with this prescription and the normal observation state's spacings, the engine's EFL 0.667163 mm gives |f1/f| = 1.642 (stated 1.64), f2/f = 38.82 (38.87), f3/f = 3.836 (3.84), D31/f = 2.00 (2.01) and FB/f = 5.426 (5.43) with FB taken as the air-reduced back focus 3.620 mm, and a paraxial trace from the stated object distance puts the image 0.7944 mm behind the last surface against the source's stated 0.792 mm

f_number.definition: the f-number the publication's parameter table states as Fno.; the source does not say which f-number convention it is, and the record does not convert it
f_number.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the publication's parameter table: Fno. 3.53 in both observation states)

field.definition: the field angle the publication states as omega; the record reads it as the full angle of view, because a half field of 80.6 deg would put the chief ray at 4.0 mm on a 0.654 mm image with a 0.667 mm focal length
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED omega = 80.6 deg (the publication's parameter table, normal observation state); the half field is DERIVED as omega/2

image_height_stated_mm.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the publication's parameter table: IH 0.654 in both observation states)
image_height_stated_mm.definition: recorded as the source states it; the source does not say whether IH is a half or a full image size, and the record does not convert it

field.convention_note: the source states omega = 80.6 deg and IH = 0.654 mm without labelling either. With the engine's 0.667163 mm focal length the paraxial full field for a 0.654 mm image height is 88.8 deg, so omega as the full angle of view implies about 10 % of barrel distortion at the field edge, which is the sign and order an endoscope objective of this class shows. Read as a half field the same numbers would need a 4.0 mm image height. The reading is stated here rather than hidden; the source itself does not resolve it

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated index (here ne, the e line). A patent table gives one index and one Abbe number per surface, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. Published catalog glasses were compared as a cross-check and are recorded under catalog_comparisons, never substituted.
materials.catalog_comparison_note: no published catalog glass is within |delta nd| <= 5e-5 and |delta vd| <= 0.05 of any of this record's nine index/Abbe pairs. The closest for the first pair is SCHOTT N-LASF31A at nd 1.88300 / vd 40.76 against the stated 1.88815 / 40.76, a difference of 5.2e-3 in index, so nothing is recorded as a comparison

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated ne; the source's Abbe numbers are recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the e line only (546.219159 nm in vacuum)

the source states no clear apertures. Each surface's clear semi-diameter is the envelope of two paraxial rays from the stated object distance: the axial marginal ray, scaled so the image-side numerical aperture gives the stated F-number 3.53 (its radius at the stop is 0.482 mm, the stop opening), and the chief ray through the stop centre to the stated image height 0.654 mm. That gives 1.287 mm at surface 1, 0.740 mm at surface 9, 0.497 mm at surface 11 and 0.682 mm at surface 17; each is edged 0.02 mm beyond the clear aperture, and the stop plate reaches 0.740 mm, the clear radius of the surface beside it. The apertures set the stop plate and the solid checks, not the first-order values

the publication gives two observation states (d0, d1, d2 all differ). The record models the normal observation state (d0 = 19.8 mm, d1 = 0.29898 mm, d2 = 2.40541 mm). The close observation state (d0 = 2.97 mm, d1 = 2.16902 mm, d2 = 0.53537 mm) is not modelled; a paraxial trace of it does not put the image on the source's printed image plane, so the normal state is the one the printed prescription and image plane belong to
the source gives no stop-plate outer radius; the plate reaches the clear semi-diameter of the surface beside it (0.740 mm)
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

surface_mapping: source surfaces 1-17 are transcribed in order; no row was merged and no zero spacing occurs
source surface 10 (Stop) is the aperture stop, carried as the STO row with the derived opening radius
the source's own surface numbering is kept in this list only; the Project numbers the rows it holds

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0
project solids reported no error-severity finding

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states no effective focal length in millimetres, so there is no pair of source-stated first-order values to compare. The engine's 0.667163 mm EFL and 0.773135 mm back focal length are recorded as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts

the source's conditional-expression table is a check the record does run: with this prescription and the normal observation state's spacings the engine's EFL gives |f1/f| = 1.642 (stated 1.64), f2/f = 38.82 (38.87), f3/f = 3.836 (3.84), D31/f = 2.00 (2.01) and FB/f = 5.426 (5.43, FB as the air-reduced back focus 3.620 mm). The transcription is therefore confirmed against the publication's own numbers, which is a stronger statement than a ratio can make about a stated focal length

the stated object distance reproduces the source's printed image plane: a paraxial trace at d0 = 19.8 mm puts the image 0.7944 mm behind the last surface against the stated 0.792 mm (0.0024 mm, 0.4 % of the 0.654 mm image height). The close observation state's d0 = 2.97 mm puts it at 0.8811 mm, which is why the normal state is the one recorded
the source's Abbe column is headed nu_d while its index column is ne; the values are recorded as stated and are not used in the model, so the mislabelling changes nothing here
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted

record_hash_method: SHA-256 over this record's JSON with the record_hash and record_hash_method members removed: json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8, no trailing newline. Recompute it from the committed record.json after parsing the JSON, not from the file's bytes.
